name: AOD-9604

b.x: About 2.6 kg of weight loss over 12 weeks on 1 mg a day by mouth, versus about 0.8 kg on placebo. That was the best arm of a 12-week trial of the AOD-9604 peptide (also called hGH fragment 177-191 or hGH frag, CAS 221231-10-3) in 300 obese adults. It was published only as a 2005 meeting abstract (Herd et al., Obesity Research). FDA's December 2024 PCAC briefing gives the rates: 0.22 kg a week versus 0.07 kg on placebo. Then the larger Phase IIb trial with 536 subjects ran for 24 weeks, added strict diet and exercise controls, and missed its primary endpoint. Metabolic Pharmaceuticals terminated the program in 2007. How AOD-9604 works is still unsettled. Unlike full-length growth hormone, it does not bind the GH receptor [4]. Blood sugar stays flat. IGF-1 stays flat. Beta-3 adrenergic receptors seem to matter, but AOD-9604 has not been shown to activate them (details under How AOD-9604 Works). FDA's 2024 briefing says the molecular target is still unknown. Community use looks different from the clinical program. Most users inject 300 to 500 mcg subcutaneously each morning on an empty stomach. Users usually justify that range by converting the 1 mg oral clinical dose with an assumed 40% oral bioavailability. FDA's 2024 briefing calls oral bioavailability unclear even in animals, and no human SC pharmacokinetic study exists. Across 50 to 150 Reddit threads in r/Peptides, the consensus is consistent: AOD-9604 is a mild add-on, not a primary fat loss tool. It performs best when stacked with CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin in a caloric deficit. Anyone expecting GLP-1-level results will be disappointed.

AOD-9604 copies the fat-burning region of growth hormone without copying anything else. The peptide corresponds to amino acids 177 through 191 of hGH, plus a tyrosine at position 176 that stabilizes the fragment. In obese Zucker rats, Ng and colleagues found oral AOD-9604 cut weight gain by more than half and raised fat-tissue lipolysis [3]. The molecular target is still unknown, per FDA's December 2024 briefing. In obese mice, 14 days of AOD-9604 cut weight gain and raised fat oxidation [4]. Plasma glycerol, a marker of lipolysis, rose too, and blood sugar did not climb the way it did on full hGH. In cell tests, AOD-9604 did not bind the GH receptor or drive cell growth through it. Beta-3 adrenergic receptors seem to be involved, but the evidence stops short of AOD-9604 activating them. Heffernan's group found it raised beta-3 receptor expression in obese mice. In beta-3 knockout mice, the 14-day course did not cut weight gain or raise lipolysis. In an acute test, though, it still raised energy expenditure and fat oxidation in those knockout mice. The authors concluded the lipolytic effect is not directly beta-3 mediated [2]. AOD-9604 also inhibits lipogenesis. Fat cells exposed to the fragment slow their conversion of circulating substrates into stored triglycerides. The dual action (accelerated breakdown plus reduced formation) produces a net shift in adipose tissue balance. Fasted morning dosing is a community convention. Users reason that insulin from a meal blunts lipolysis, so they keep it low around the injection. None of the six human trials compared fed and fasted dosing, so the rule is untested for AOD-9604.
AOD-9604 benefits center on targeted fat metabolism without the hormonal baggage of full-length growth hormone.

A 12-week trial in 300 obese adults works out to about 2.6 kg of weight loss at 1 mg oral, versus about 0.8 kg on placebo. FDA's December 2024 PCAC briefing took those rates (0.22 vs 0.07 kg a week) from a 2005 meeting abstract. Waist circumference fell faster than placebo at every dose.
No blood sugar disruption. AOD-9604 does not bind the GH receptor, so insulin sensitivity, fasting glucose, and HbA1c stay unaffected. Users managing metabolic concerns prefer this profile.

Zero IGF-1 elevation. In the human trials, serum IGF-1 did not change versus placebo (Stier 2013 safety review of six trials). The growth and acromegalic features of exogenous GH don't apply; the 12-week oral trial's cancer reports are covered under Side Effects.

Stacks well with GH secretagogues. The most common community protocol pairs AOD-9604 with CJC-1295 and Ipamorelin; direct lipolysis plus GH-axis pulsing is why this trinity stack dominates r/Peptides threads.
No receptor desensitization reported. Clinical and community data both show consistent response across 12-week cycles. Users don't need to escalate doses over time.

The Phase IIb trial of 536 subjects over 24 weeks produced the largest safety dataset. Headache was the most frequently reported adverse event in the oral formulation groups. Four of the six human trials used oral capsules or tablets, and two gave single IV infusions (Stier 2013). Zero published human safety data exist for subcutaneous injection. Every subcutaneous safety claim is extrapolated from oral and single-dose IV data. That distinction matters because local tissue reactions, immunogenicity potential, and injection site effects cannot be inferred from swallowed capsules. FDA PCAC specifically cited manufacturing impurity risks and immunogenicity concerns for compounded injectable forms in their December 2024 review. Published adverse events from the human trials (Stier 2013, a sponsor-funded safety review of about 900 adults): Headache: most common. Adverse events overall ran at rates similar to placebo, mostly mild or moderate. Digestive events (diarrhea, flatulence, nausea) came next. Headache, diarrhea and flatulence were more frequent at 54 mg a day in a 7-day trial. Five people had serious adverse events in the 12-week oral trial, which gave 1 to 30 mg a day or placebo to 300 adults. Per FDA's December 2024 briefing, the 20 mg arm had basal cell carcinoma, a lipoma and squamous cell carcinoma. Breast cancer came at 5 mg and malignant melanoma at 10 mg. The investigator judged none related to AOD-9604, noting no cancers at the top 30 mg dose. FDA flagged the cancers as a concern; the reports held too little detail to judge whether AOD-9604 played a part. Two smaller trials, per the same FDA briefing, logged events judged possibly related to AOD-9604. In an oral dose-escalation study, the 54 mg dose drew two serious adverse events: diarrhea, judged possibly related, and pneumonia, judged unrelated. In an IV study, one case of severe chest tightness at 50 mcg/kg was judged possibly related. So were five reports of mild or moderate euphoria, with none on placebo. No clinically meaningful changes in blood glucose, insulin or IGF-1 were seen versus placebo. Community-reported side effects from subcutaneous use (r/Peptides, approximately 50 to 150 threads): Injection site reactions are the primary complaint. Redness, mild swelling, and induration at the injection site affect most new users. These are cosmetic and self-resolving. Diluting to a lower concentration, warming the vial to room temperature, and slowing injection speed all help. Lipodystrophy at injection sites has been reported with poor site rotation. Rotate across four abdominal quadrants minimum. Quality risk is a real factor. AOD-9604 is a 15-residue peptide requiring precise disulfide bridge formation during synthesis. Purity varies widely across unregulated research-chemical products. Low-purity preparations carry higher immunogenicity and local reaction risk. Only lot-specific HPLC and LC-MS data showing 98% or higher purity can confirm a batch. AOD-9604 is WADA-prohibited (category S2, Growth Hormone Fragments) and detectable via mass spectrometry [5]. The Essendon Football Club scandal in 2012 involved roughly 34 AFL players who received AOD-9604 injections; several faced bans. AOD-9604 has not been studied in pregnancy or breastfeeding. No pediatric data exist. Active malignancy is a contraindication because effects on tumor growth have not been evaluated. Known hypersensitivity to the peptide or excipients is an absolute contraindication. When to stop: discontinue if injection site nodules develop, if local reaction severity increases over successive weeks (potential immunogenicity signal), or if unexpected systemic symptoms appear that resolve during off-cycle periods. Any hypoglycemia symptoms when stacking with GLP-1 agonists or secretagogues warrant immediate discontinuation and medical evaluation.
Common Issues & Solutions

No results at 300 mcg: Verify fasted state is strict (no food, coffee with cream, BCAAs for ≥2h prior). Community protocols assume insulin blunts the effect, though none of the six human trials tested fed versus fasted dosing.
No results despite fasting: no study has tested SC dosing, so no SC dose has a proven effect. Community protocols use 300 to 500 mcg and call it a non-response after 8 weeks at 400 mcg.

Injection site redness/swelling: Dilute to lower concentration (add more BAC water), warm vial to room temperature before injection, and slow the injection rate. Reactions are typically cosmetic and self-resolving.

Minimal fat loss vs GLP-1 expectations: AOD-9604 is not a GLP-1 agonist. The Phase IIb trial failed. Realistic outcomes are 0.5–2 kg over 12 weeks in caloric deficit: not the 15–22% body weight reductions seen with semaglutide/tirzepatide.

Uncertain about real vs. placebo effect: Track with DEXA or circumference measurements, not scale weight alone. AOD-9604 does not cause fluid retention or muscle gain, so scale changes directly reflect composition shifts.
Double-check with AI
Pregnancy or breastfeeding: no safety data in these populations
Active malignancy or history of cancer: effects on tumor growth not studied
Known hypersensitivity to AOD-9604 or any excipients
Children and adolescents under 18: not studied in pediatric populations
Insulin and oral hypoglycemics: although AOD-9604 does not directly affect blood sugar, monitor glucose when combining with diabetes medications
Thyroid medications: fat metabolism changes may alter thyroid hormone requirements; monitor levels
Other lipolytic agents (e.g., growth hormone, clenbuterol): potential additive effects on fat mobilization; use with caution
Anticoagulants: no known interaction, but as with all injectable peptides, monitor for injection site bruising

AOD-9604 is not FDA-approved for any therapeutic indication. The pharmaceutical development program (Metabolic Pharmaceuticals, Australia) was terminated in 2007 after Phase IIb failure. The compound holds GRAS status strictly as an oral food additive. That designation does not apply to injectable use. FDA PCAC voted in December 2024 to recommend that AOD-9604 not be included on the 503A Bulks List for pharmacy compounding. Formal rulemaking is pending. If finalized, compounded injectable AOD-9604 from 503A pharmacies would become unavailable. Research-chemical supply remains legal for non-human research purposes in most US jurisdictions. AOD-9604 is WADA-prohibited under category S2 (Peptide Hormones, Growth Factors, Related Substances, and Mimetics). It is detectable via mass spectrometry (Drug Testing and Analysis 2015) [5]. Competitive athletes must not use it. This content is for informational and research purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.
Evidence grade: Phase 2 trial (Peptide Evidence Gap, October 2026)

faqs.q: Does AOD-9604 actually work for fat loss?
faqs.a: A 12-week trial in 300 obese adults reported weight loss of 0.22 kg a week at 1 mg oral, about 2.6 kg in total. Placebo lost 0.07 kg a week, and the trial appeared only as a 2005 meeting abstract. The larger Phase IIb trial (~500 subjects, 24 weeks) failed its primary endpoint when rigorous diet and exercise were incorporated, and the pharmaceutical program was terminated in 2007. Community results at SC doses are variable and modest; do not compare expected outcomes to GLP-1 agonists.

faqs.q: What does the GRAS status actually mean for injectable use?
faqs.a: The GRAS determination applies to oral ingestion as a food additive. It says nothing about the safety of injectable use, which is how the compound is predominantly used in the research community. Four of the 6 clinical trials were oral and two gave single IV doses. No trial tested subcutaneous injection, so its safety is inferred.

faqs.q: Why do community SC doses (300–500 mcg) differ from the 1 mg oral clinical dose?
faqs.a: No study has tested subcutaneous dosing, so the 300 to 500 mcg range comes from user practice, not a trial. The human trials gave AOD-9604 by mouth (0.25 to 54 mg a day) or as single IV doses (Stier 2013). FDA's December 2024 briefing found no human pharmacokinetic study for any route and calls oral bioavailability unclear, even in animals; a pig study's numbers worked out to an impossible 170%. So no SC dose can be matched to the 1 mg oral trial dose.

faqs.q: Is AOD-9604 legal and will it show on drug tests?
faqs.a: As a research chemical, possession is legal in most jurisdictions. However, it is WADA-prohibited and detectable. The Essendon Football Club (AFL) doping scandal (2012) involved ~34 players injected with AOD-9604; several received bans.

Fasted morning dosing is the community standard. Inject on an empty stomach and wait 30–60 minutes before eating. Users reason that insulin from a meal blunts fat breakdown. None of the six human trials compared fed and fasted dosing, so the rule is a community convention rather than a tested finding.
AOD-9604 typically comes in 5mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.
